text.p: South Africa is close to reaching a trade agreement with Zimbabwe, its largest trading partner in Africa, President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday.

Mandela, on a state visit to Zimbabwe, told a breakfast meeting attended by Zimbabwean business leaders that the two governments were working hard to resolve differences that have held up a comprehensive agreement over the last three years.

He said a pact on agricultural and other products could be concluded soon, following a breakthrough achieved in March when Zimbabwean clothing and textiles regained access to South Africa after three years of exclusion by protective tariffs.

"Following a meeting between (South African Trade and Industry Minister Alec) Erwin and (Zimbabwe Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan) Shamuyarira last month, the outstanding issues concerning agricultural and other products are close to conclusion," Mandela said.

The trade issues include electrical goods and farm export subsidies, brought to the fore by recent protests by South African producers that Zimbabwe planned to dump more than one million tonnes of its current maize surplus.

"Sooner rather than later, we are confident that our economic relations will prove to be as cordial, cooperative and mutually beneficial as our relations in all other spheres," Mandela said to applause.

Mandela, who ends a three-day state visit to Zimbabwe on Wednesday, told a rally in southern Masvingo province on Tuesday that he would like to develop the "right" trade relationship with Zimbabwe, which complains that it is getting a raw deal.

During a question and answer session with Zimbabwean business leaders on Wednesday, Mandela told the president of the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries, Jonee Blanchfield, that there was a need for patience in the trade negotiations.
"We came into power only three years ago and we cannot be expected to have solved all these problems," he said to suggestions a trade agreement was long overdue.

Negotiations to update an expired 1964 trade agreement have gone on since 1992. Despite vehement denials, Zimbabwean business and government leaders have consistently accused South Africa of dragging its feet in concluding the agreement.

South Africa is Zimbabwe's largest trading partner in Africa but the trade is heavily weighted in South Africa's favour. In 1995, trade between the two nations totalled Z$10 billion (U.S.$885 million).
